title: A covariance-aware reference reduced fixed-readout guarantees in 93 selected Allen two-input models
abstract: We tested fixed positive readouts across first and late 50 Hz response summaries in 93 selected Allen cortical two-input models. We compared each readout with an optimum that knows the actual noise covariance. For two inputs, a proof reduces the full correlation interval to its endpoints. At an assumed absolute correlation cap of 0.5, the best fixed readout fell below 80 percent efficiency in 38 models. A ratio of worst-case signal-to-noise values fell below that level in four of the same models. Restricting correlations to the interval from zero to 0.5 left only five failures. Thus the large difference depends strongly on allowing negative correlations. An independent quadratic check agreed within 1.89e-11 efficiency units in all primary models at cap 0.5. Input covariance was not measured. Medians assigned as means, fixed marginal summaries, separate input trials and selected slices prevent a neuronal decoding claim. Code, proof, aggregate evidence and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Solid curves show the same-covariance efficiency guarantee. Dotted curves show the ratio of worst-case squared signal-to-noise values. Correlation caps are model assumptions.

citations.reason: Reuses selection and MIT solver functions. Replaces the ratio of robust optima with a guarantee against the same-covariance optimum; restricts groups to exactly two inputs.
